lead.headline: Congress Pushes Bitcoin Reserve Bill and Crypto Tax Overhaul as Regulators Fill Rulemaking Void
lead.tldr: Two parallel tracks are accelerating: legislative codification of a U.S. strategic Bitcoin reserve and a bipartisan tax framework for digital assets, while the SEC and CFTC move unilaterally as comprehensive market structure legislation stalls. The signal is institutionalization via statute, not just executive action.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the legislative-regulatory gap is becoming the defining investment variable for U.S. exposure.

top_signals.title: House committee moves to codify Trump's Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
top_signals.summary: A U.S. House committee has advanced legislation to establish a strategic bitcoin reserve. This move aims to codify the proposal for the United States to maintain permanent bitcoin holdings.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Codifying the strategic Bitcoin reserve through committee legislation reduces reversal risk beyond executive order, creating a more durable bid floor that institutional allocators can underwrite against.

top_signals.title: US lawmakers advance bill to lock Trump’s Bitcoin reserve into lawThe legislation would effectively codify Trump’s Bitcoin reserve policy, locking up Bitcoin acquired through civil and criminal forfeiture for 20 years.
top_signals.summary: US lawmakers are advancing legislation to codify a strategic Bitcoin reserve by law. The bill proposes locking Bitcoin acquired via civil and criminal forfeitures for a period of 20 years.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 20-year lock-up mechanism on forfeited Bitcoin transforms a temporary policy into a structural supply sink, directly repricing scarcity assumptions for long-dated Treasury and endowment models.

top_signals.title: 'Go time': SEC, CFTC prepare to push crypto rules as Clarity Act stalls in Senate
top_signals.summary: The SEC and CFTC are preparing to implement their own cryptocurrency regulations as the Clarity Act faces delays in the Senate. CFTC Chair Mike Selig indicated that the agency is ready to finalize and deploy rules for the digital asset sector.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Regulatory bifurcation—agencies advancing rules while Congress dithers—introduces compliance fragmentation risk that favors incumbents with legal infrastructure over startups operating across jurisdictions.

top_signals.title: US House tax committee advances crypto tax overhaul in 38–5 voteA bipartisan House committee vote advanced legislation that would reshape federal tax rules for stablecoins, staking, crypto lending and digital asset transactions., US House tax committee advances crypto tax overhaul in 38–5 vote
top_signals.summary: A US House tax committee has passed a bipartisan bill in a 38–5 vote to overhaul federal tax rules for digital assets. The legislation aims to reshape how stablecoins, staking, and crypto lending are taxed.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A 38–5 bipartisan vote on tax treatment signals that stablecoin and staking normalization has crossed political threshold, reducing the discount rate on yield-generating protocols with U.S. user bases.

top_signals.title: Circle launches Arc mainnet with BlackRock and Visa among validators, mints 10 billion ARC tokens
top_signals.summary: Circle has launched the Arc mainnet, featuring industry giants BlackRock and Visa as validators. The company has completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens, though a public launch date is not yet determined.
top_signals.why_it_matters: BlackRock and Visa validating a Circle chain validates the thesis that institutional infrastructure players are vertically integrating into settlement layers, compressing standalone validator economics.

deals.summary: Tare has raised $13 million in funding led by Blockchain Capital to develop a platform for managing private credit transactions on the blockchain. The startup aims to streamline credit operations to improve returns for both lenders and borrowers.

on_the_radar.title: Deutsche Bank plans bitcoin, ether custody for institutional clients in Europe
on_the_radar.summary: Deutsche Bank is planning to launch a digital asset custody service for institutional clients in Europe later this year. The service will initially support Bitcoin, Ether, and specific stablecoins.

on_the_radar.title: UK FCA sets crypto authorization guidance ahead of September application window38m, UK FCA sets crypto authorization guidance ahead of September application windowThe FCA’s new guidance outlines which crypto activities may require authorization as firms prepare for the UK’s incoming digital asset regulatory regime.
on_the_radar.summary: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has released new guidance on crypto authorization requirements. This prepares firms for a formal application window opening in September as the UK establishes its digital asset regulatory regime.

on_the_radar.title: ECB seeks online merchants for 2027 digital euro pilot19m, ECB seeks online merchants for 2027 digital euro pilotEuro-area online and mobile merchants can apply until Oct. 27 to test beta digital euro payments in a 12-month pilot.
on_the_radar.summary: The European Central Bank is recruiting online and mobile merchants to participate in a 12-month beta pilot for the digital euro starting in 2027. This initiative aims to test the practical application of the CBDC in real-world payment scenarios.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin, ether swing after unanimous quarter-point Fed rate hike as Warsh takes aim at inflation
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin and Ether experienced price volatility following a unanimous quarter-point interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. The move marks the first rate increase in over three years as officials continue to target inflation.

on_the_radar.title: Anchorage expands institutional custody to Etherlink, tokenized uranium
on_the_radar.summary: Anchorage Digital Bank has expanded its institutional custody services to include the Tezos layer-2 network, Etherlink. This expansion includes support for seven different assets, most notably tokenized physical uranium.

on_the_radar.title: Ethiopia cuts Bitcoin miners’ power by 77% amid hydropower shortage: Report19m, Ethiopia cuts Bitcoin miners’ power by 77% amid hydropower shortage: ReportBitcoin miners generated 35% of the state-owned power producer’s revenue last year, but declining reservoir inflows led the utility to prioritize households and manufacturers.
on_the_radar.summary: Ethiopia has reduced power supply to Bitcoin miners by 77% due to a severe hydropower shortage. The state-owned utility is prioritizing residential and manufacturing sectors over mining operations despite miners contributing 35% of its revenue last year.

on_the_radar.title: Underdog sues Connecticut to stop sports prediction market crackdown
on_the_radar.summary: Underdog has filed a lawsuit against the state of Connecticut to challenge a crackdown on sports prediction markets. This follows cease-and-desist orders issued to several platforms, including Polymarket and Coinbase.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto and Blockchain Venture Capital
on_the_radar.summary: Venture capital activity in the crypto and blockchain sector saw a rebound during the second quarter. This recovery was primarily driven by later-stage financing, although the creation of new funds remained weak.

linkedin_post:
The House moved on two tracks this week. One committee voted to lock forfeited Bitcoin into a 20-year strategic reserve. Another passed a tax overhaul 38–5, treating stablecoins and staking like instruments that actually exist. Both advanced with bipartisan margins that the CLARITY Act never commanded.

We have seen this shape before. When agencies move because comprehensive legislation stalls, the rules that get written become the rules that survive. SEC and CFTC chairs are now saying explicitly what was implied: they will fill the vacuum themselves. That is not a failure of process. It is a different kind of institutionalization, one that fragments compliance obligations across two regulators instead of one statute.

For founders, the cost structure changes. Legal infrastructure becomes a moat earlier in the lifecycle. For investors, the repricing is sector-specific: U.S.-facing yield protocols just saw their tax overhang compress, while cross-chain infrastructure faces a more expensive compliance stack.

The reserve bill matters most if it survives markup. The tax bill matters most if the Senate does not gut the staking provisions. We are watching whether the 20-year lock-up survives conference, and whether any senator actually objects to treating staking rewards as created property rather than income. If neither gets diluted, the U.S. is underwriting a structural bid floor and a normalized yield curve in the same quarter. That is a repricing event. Not inevitable.
